proposals.title: Review Assurance Floor Execution Plan
proposals.decision: Lattice should add a mandatory review assurance floor for code-changing stories: ordinary code diffs require at least one review round before DONE, failure or bug signals escalate to three local single-host rounds, and high-risk lifecycle/gate/Authority/process-fact work keeps the stronger three-round two-host or explicit degraded-single-host path.
proposals.context: A small development task can look low risk during PLAN but still ship a bug when it reaches DONE with no review floor. Existing review escalation is threshold-triggered by first REVIEW round countable findings, which is useful but does not prevent zero-review code closure. This plan documents the missing floor and the escalation rule without implementing runtime code in this story.
proposals.scope: Applies to future Lattice CLI lifecycle policy and DONE closure design for code-changing stories. This document is a planning and policy artifact only; runtime DONE oracle implementation, storage fields, and exact row ids are future work.
nonGoals: Do not force every code-changing story into three rounds by default.
Do not weaken existing review_escalation_status, decision_doc_quorum_check, or DONE gates.
Do not claim local 3x1 review is two-host independent review.
Do not claim Authority completion without verified Authority Server gate_decision receipts.
Do not implement runtime gate code in this story.
proposals.chosenApproach: Introduce a review assurance floor: zero-review code DONE is invalid; clean ordinary code requires at least one review round; real failure signals such as validation fail, bug, verified reviewer finding, post-DONE regression, or repeated rework make 3x1 local single-host audit sticky for closure; high-risk gate/Authority/lifecycle/process-fact work still requires 3x2 unless explicit degraded-single-host evidence is recorded.

alternatives.name: Force every code change through three local single-host rounds
pros: Stronger than one-round review for every code diff
cons: Over-applies heavy review to clean small changes
Raises token and time cost without requiring a real failure signal

alternatives.name: Keep current threshold-triggered review escalation only
pros: No new policy or implementation work
cons: Does not solve zero-review code DONE
Misses low-risk-looking tasks that only reveal bugs after implementation

alternatives.name: Require full 3x2 for every code change
cons: Too expensive for ordinary small code changes
Can block local development when a second host is unavailable

operationalRules: If a story has no material code diff, it may use the existing docs/typo/annotation policy for one-round low-risk review.
If a story has a material code diff, DONE must require at least one review round over the current material hash.

If a story records a validation fail, bug, verified reviewer finding, post-DONE regression, or repeated rework signal, DONE must require three rounds x one local host unless stronger policy requires 3x2.
Failure-triggered 3x1 escalation must be sticky for the story material until DONE or an explicit approved fallback supersedes it.
Lifecycle, gate, Authority, review, and process-fact work remains high-risk and should use three rounds x two hosts, or an explicit degraded-single-host fallback when policy allows.
Local host verdicts and degraded fallback evidence are Non-authority evidence and must not set authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, or productionDone.
Future implementation must fail closed on stale material hash, missing host identity, missing prompt or validation binding, and duplicate/self-claimed assurance.
verificationRequirements: A future smoke test proves an ordinary code-diff story cannot reach DONE with zero review rounds.
A future smoke test proves a clean ordinary code-diff story can close after one valid review round.
A future smoke test proves validation failure or bug evidence makes 3x1 required and sticky before DONE.
A future smoke test proves high-risk lifecycle/gate/Authority/process-fact stories still require 3x2 or explicit degraded-single-host evidence.
A future smoke test proves 3x1 evidence reports assuranceLevel=degraded-single-host and never claims Authority Server receipt-backed completion.
risks: Over-escalation could waste tokens if every source diff is treated as failure-triggered.
Under-escalation could persist if failure signals are not captured in a gate-consumed artifact.
Confusing 3x1 with two-host independence would overclaim review assurance.
Confusing local host verdicts with Authority receipts would violate the Authority boundary.
